records.title: On Elliott's conjecture and applications
records.identity_verification: Primary arXiv record and actual PDF title page inspected.
records.exact_scope: For arbitrary unit-disc multiplicative f1,f2, one fixed f1 nonpretentious gives ordinary binary correlation cancellation on a set X with upper logarithmic density 1, for distinct fixed shifts.
records.hypothesis: Nonpretentious means for every fixed Dirichlet character chi and every fixed real t, D(f1,chi*n^{it};infinity)=infinity. This is weaker than requiring inf_{|t|<=N} D(f1,chi*n^{it};N)->infinity for every fixed chi.
records.sharpness_caution: Proposition 1.3 gives a nonpretentious function whose absolute two-point correlation tends to 1 along a set of full upper log-log density. The weak hypothesis is not interchangeable with the corrected growing-twist hypothesis and does not permit an every-cutoff conclusion.

records.title: Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers
records.identity_verification: Primary arXiv record and actual PDF title page inspected.
records.general_hypotheses: 1-bounded multiplicative g1,g2; 1<=L<=log X; either the stated quantitative equidistribution axiom plus technical prime-value condition, or delta_N=0 with exp(M(g1;X^2,(log X)^(1/125))) >> L. The conclusion is outside E subset [sqrt X,X] with logarithmic measure/log X << L^(-c).
records.liouville_consequence: For some small absolute c>0 and integers a1,a2,b1,b2 between 1 and (log N)^c with a1*b2!=a2*b1, the normalized ordinary Liouville correlation is <<(log N)^(-c) for all N outside E; E obeys (1/log X) integral_[1,X] intersect E dt/t <<(log X)^(-c).
records.comparison_limit: This prior Liouville estimate permits slowly growing positive coefficients but retains an exceptional scale set. The release's inspected affine Liouville assertion fixes coefficients (also permits b_i=0) and removes the exceptional scale set. Neither scope should be casually described as containing every aspect of the other.
